name: International (ICAO/IATA)
regulator: ICAO Technical Instructions, as published by IATA

binOpening.note: Traveller-reported, not a manufacturer figure, and reports disagree — see the two competing claims scoped to this type. Recorded at the larger reported size so the geometry check is not falsely strict.
Traveller-reported figure for mid-size regional jet bins. Treat as indicative.

title: PackSafe — Lithium Batteries
excerpt: Spare (uninstalled) lithium ion and lithium metal batteries, including power banks and cell phone battery charging cases, must be carried in carry-on baggage only. … The battery terminals must be protected from short circuit.

title: PackSafe — Portable Electronic Devices Containing Batteries
excerpt: Devices containing lithium metal or lithium ion batteries (laptops, smartphones, tablets, etc.) should be carried in carry-on baggage. … When portable electronic devices powered by lithium batteries are in checked baggage, they must be completely powered off and protected to prevent unintentional activation or damage.

title: Safe Travel with Lithium Batteries
excerpt: Up to 100 watt-hours (Wh): generally allowed in carry-on baggage. 100–160 Wh: may be allowed with airline approval. Over 160 Wh: usually not permitted on passenger aircraft. … Never place spare batteries or power banks in checked baggage.

title: Battery or Fuel-Powered Items
excerpt: Spare lithium batteries are allowed in carry-on baggage only with batteries individually protected to prevent short circuit … no more than two (2) spares between 100 and 160-watt hours are allowed.

title: Carry-On Baggage
excerpt: Passengers traveling on Delta Connection flights, including flights with 50 seats or less, are only permitted to carry personal items on board the aircraft due to limited overhead space.

title: Restricted items in bags — Special Notice: Generator and battery restrictions
excerpt: Large portable power banks and lithium-ion battery-powered generators are not allowed as carry-on or checked items.

title: Interline Considerations on Baggage Standards (Resolution 302 guidance)
excerpt: Where published baggage provisions differ between participating carriers, the provisions of the Most Significant Carrier apply to the whole checked portion of the journey.

title: Traveller thread: 21 × 14 × 7 carry-on on the CRJ-200
excerpt: Reports of the largest bag that goes into a CRJ-200 bin, given as roughly 21 × 14 × 7 inches.

title: Traveller thread: regional-jet bins and the bag that would not fit
excerpt: Reports of smaller regional-jet bins, given as roughly 18 × 13 × 8 inches.

subject: spareBatteryCabinOnly
quote: Spare (uninstalled) lithium ion and lithium metal batteries … must be carried in carry-on baggage only.
note: Also requires that spares be removed and kept with the passenger if the carry-on is gate-checked — which is exactly what happens on a 50-seat regional jet.

subject: spareBatteryApprovalAboveWh
quote: Lithium ion (rechargeable) batteries are limited to a rating of 100 watt hours (Wh) per battery.

subject: spareBatteryMaxWh
quote: With airline approval, passengers may also carry up to two spare larger lithium ion batteries (exceeding 101–160 Wh).
note: Marked as a ceiling: no operator may permit more, so it caps whatever the carrier overlays resolve to.

subject: spareBatteryMaxCount
quote: There is a limit of two spare batteries per person for the larger lithium ion batteries … (exceeding 101–160 Wh per battery).
note: Scoped above 100 Wh deliberately. The same page says there is no quantity limit for ordinary cells, so an unscoped version of this claim would wrongly cap a passenger at two phone batteries.

subject: powerBankTerminalProtectionRequired
quote: The battery terminals must be protected from short circuit.

subject: spareMustLeaveGateCheckedBag
quote: When a carry-on bag is checked at the gate or at planeside, all spare lithium batteries and power banks must be removed from the bag and kept with the passenger in the aircraft cabin.

subject: spareMustLeaveGateCheckedBag
quote: When a carry-on bag is checked at the gate or at planeside, any spare lithium batteries must be removed from the bag and kept with the passenger in the aircraft cabin.
note: Two FAA pages state the same rule in almost the same words. Kept as two claims rather than one so the resolver reports "unanimous" rather than "sole-source" — a rule stated twice by the regulator is worth knowing about.

subject: spareBatteryApprovalAboveWh
quote: 100–160 Wh: may be allowed with airline approval.

subject: spareBatteryMaxWh
quote: Over 160 Wh: usually not permitted on passenger aircraft.

subject: spareBatteryCabinOnly
quote: Never place spare batteries or power banks in checked baggage.

subject: spareBatteryMaxWh
quote: lithium ion batteries that contain a maximum of 160-watt hours per battery

subject: spareBatteryMaxCount
quote: no more than two (2) spares between 100 and 160-watt hours are allowed

subject: spareBatteryMaxWh
quote: No more than two power banks may be carried per person, and they may not exceed an aggregate total of 100 Wh each
note: "an aggregate total of 100 Wh each" is ambiguous: it can be read as 100 Wh per unit, or as 100 Wh across both. Recorded as the per-unit reading because that is the stricter of the two and the one a gate agent is likeliest to apply — but recorded as uncertain, and there is an open proposed ruling asking a human to settle it rather than pretending the sentence is clear.

subject: spareBatteryMaxCount
quote: No more than two power banks may be carried per person
note: Applies at any watt-hour rating, unlike the regulator’s two-spare limit which only bites above 100 Wh. This is the carrier being stricter in a way the FAA page explicitly anticipates.

subject: spareBatteryCabinOnly
quote: Spare lithium batteries are allowed in carry-on baggage only

subject: carryOnMaxDimensionsMm
quote: Individual length, width and height measurements may not exceed 22" x 14" x 9" … include any handles or wheels

subject: carryOnPieceCount
quote: 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item free of charge

subject: personalItemAllowed
quote: 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item free of charge

subject: carryOnPieceCount
quote: Passengers traveling on Delta Connection flights, including flights with 50 seats or less, are only permitted to carry personal items on board
note: Scoped by seat count because that is how the source writes it. Any 50-seat type added to the dataset inherits this automatically.

subject: carryOnMaxDimensionsMm
quote: Reported largest bag to go into a CRJ-200 bin: about 21 × 14 × 7 inches.

subject: carryOnMaxDimensionsMm
quote: Reported regional-jet bin capacity: about 18 × 13 × 8 inches.
note: Deeper but shorter than the other report. Neither fits inside the other, so the resolver refuses to order them and asks for a ruling instead of splitting the difference.

subject: spareBatteryMaxWh
rationale: Delta caps batteries at 160 Wh generally but writes "they may not exceed an aggregate total of 100 Wh each" about power banks specifically. The sentence can be read two ways. Proposing the per-unit reading at 100 Wh: it is the stricter one, and a traveller turned away at the gate is worse off than one who left a power bank at home. Needs a named person to sign before it binds.

subject: carryOnMaxDimensionsMm
rationale: Two traveller reports of CRJ-200 bin capacity, one longer and one deeper, so neither contains the other and the resolver correctly refuses to pick. Proposing the 18 × 13 × 8 reading: depth is the axis that actually stops a bag entering these bins. Both figures are traveller-reported and neither should be treated as authoritative — the better fix is a manufacturer or carrier source.

label: JFK → ATL → TYS — one ticket, two different sets of rules
teachingPoint: Both segments say Delta on the boarding pass. The second is flown by Endeavor Air on a 50-seat CRJ-200, where Delta’s own carry-on page permits personal items only. A bag that is perfectly legal on the way out cannot come into the cabin on the way home — and once it is gate-checked, the FAA requires every spare battery to come out of it first.

label: SEA → AMS — widebody, camera and drone kit
teachingPoint: A single long-haul segment, but the kit is the interesting part. A 137 Wh cell needs the operating carrier’s approval; three of them break the two-spare limit; and the identical 137 Wh sold as a power bank is refused outright because Delta caps power banks lower than it caps camera batteries.

label: DFW → ORD — American, with a portable power station
teachingPoint: The case where structured claims run out. American’s notice bans "large portable power banks" without defining large, so there is no number to compute with. The regulatory ceiling still answers the question, and the Knowledge Base supplies the carrier prose that no GROQ query could have returned.
